name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 11 points on the PVI
Incumbent Lori Trahan running with a large financial advantage, roughly $1.8 million on hand versus under $6,000 for the Republican
Prediction markets price Trahan near 95% to win
No public general-election polling available for this race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Trahan: an 11-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a fundraising gap of more than 200-to-1, with markets also pricing her as an overwhelming favorite. With no polls or expert ratings to add nuance, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually competitive race, or significant outside spending on Grossi's behalf, would be the first sign of movement in this low-attention contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lori Trahan seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about 11 points. She enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $1.6 million and holding about $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised only about $7,000. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which give Trahan roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The combination of incumbency, the district's partisan lean, and the lopsided resource gap makes an upset unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
